column3: Snowflake. The hexagon is one growing ice crystal, and its six-fold symmetry is the board's own. Dendrites branch along the lattice's three natural directions (vertical and +-30 degrees); frost glints travel along them. The time is frozen into the crystal: numerals made of ice needles along the 60-degree lattice (hours carved into the inner crystal, minutes grown on the arms, or another arrangement that keeps the symmetry alive). Minute turn: the changed digit sublimates into drifting vapour sparkles that refreeze needle by needle into the new one. Hour: the whole flake melts into a trembling droplet at the centre and re-nucleates as a new, different flake (seeded by the hour). Palette: blue-black night, ice cyan, white glints, perhaps a warm window glow behind.

Sand mandala. Tibetan monks pour coloured sand into a sacred mandala, and the hexagon's 10 concentric rings are its bands (ring k has 6k LEDs: ring 2 = 12 for hours, ring 10 = 60 for minutes). The minute track is laid grain by grain in the outer ring by a chak-pur funnel that travels round; the hour is a sand-drawn numeral or emblem in the heart; patterns in the middle rings are built up and rotate. Grains glint and settle continuously. Minute turn: the funnel trickles the next segment and the inner patterns turn a step. Hour: the ritual destruction, where the whole mandala is swept spiralling into the centre into one heap of mixed colour, and the monks begin again. Mineral palette (lapis, cinnabar, saffron, malachite) on dark.

Prism. The big triangle IS a glass prism (think Dark Side of the Moon): a thin white beam enters from the left, refracts inside and fans out to the right as a spectrum. The time is written by light: the dispersed rays focus into caustic numerals, or internal reflections trace the digits, or each digit is a spectral band; find the most beautiful version. Minute turn: the prism rotates a few degrees, the spectrum sweeps across and refocuses into the new digits (Snell's law, smooth). Hour: a full spin, rainbow sweeping the whole face, then settling. The four boards share one continuous lattice.

Volcano at night. The big triangle stands apex-up as a volcano: a smoke plume and stars above the crater, magma glowing inside. Lava rivers flow down the flanks and pool into the numerals; crust darkens and cracks to show glowing seams; embers float. Minute turn: a rumble, a small eruption from the crater, and fresh lava runs down to rewrite the changed digit while the old one cools to black rock. Hour: a full eruption, a lava fountain, an ash cloud lit from below, then the new hour flows in. kit.blackbody gives the lava palette. The four boards share one continuous lattice.

Koi stream. The long trapezoid ribbon is a stream seen from above: water caustics, lily pads drifting, koi (vermilion, gold, white with red patches) swimming. The koi school together and their bodies curve into the numerals: the digits are made of fish, scales glinting. Minute turn: a pebble or a crumb sends ripples; the fish of the changed digit scatter and regroup into the new one. Hour: a golden koi leaps up the waterfall at one end and becomes a dragon that sweeps along the ribbon (the koi-to-dragon legend), leaving the new hour. Characters drawn with care; legible at real size. The five boards share one continuous lattice.

Hex island. Seven hexagons are seven tiles of a tiny living board-game world (think Catan): forest, wheat, mountains with a mine, a lake, pasture with sheep, a village, and the seams between boards are the tile borders. Weather and day/night move across it (the sun follows the real time). The time is told by the world and must read from across a room: e.g. the hour built by tiny settlers out of roads and houses on one ring of tiles, minutes by something else. Minute turn: settlers carry pieces, a ship sails in; hour: two giant dice tumble across the board and the robber pawn moves. Big canvas (2317 LEDs), 10 A budget.

Porthole. The octagon is a brass submarine porthole looking into the deep sea. In the dark water an anglerfish swims, its lure a moving light; bioluminescent plankton glow where disturbed and arrange themselves into the numerals (the light is the font). Marine snow drifts down. Minute turn: a jellyfish or the anglerfish passes through the digit, stirring the plankton, which re-settle into the new number. Hour: the sub surfaces, sunlight floods in, waves wash over the glass, then it dives again. 16x16 with cut corners is small: letterforms must be designed for it.

Laundromat. Three octagons are the round doors of three front-loading washing machines at night. Inside, laundry tumbles in suds: the hour in machine 1 and minutes in machine 2, the digits made of clothes (a long striped sock bent into a numeral, a shirt's pattern...), while machine 3 runs a cycle that shows the seconds or minute progress. Constant tumbling, bubbles, water sloshing. Minute turn: a short spin whirls the clothes into a blur and they flop down as the new digit. Hour: all three finish together with a rinse of bubbles and a little ding, doors fogging. Playful and cute. The three boards share one continuous lattice (with the octagons' cut corners).

Gumball machine. The octagon is the glass globe full of coloured gumballs (physical-feeling: jostling, settling); the 32x8 strip below is the red base. Each minute a coin drops, the crank turns, and gumballs roll down a chute into the base, where they settle as the minute digits (gumball dot letterforms), pushing out the old ones; the hour is spelled by gumballs inside the globe. Hour: the globe refills in a pouring cascade. Mixed pitches: the globe is 4 mm frosted LEDs, the base 3 mm clear ones; the hand-off between them is the fun.

Rubik's cube. A 3D Rubik's cube in isometric view on the 40x40 canvas, properly shaded. Its stickers spell the time: hour on one face, minutes on another (choose the cube order so stickers are big enough for pixel digits), and the cube slowly turns in 3D between minutes. Minute turn: a real sequence of slice rotations, animated in 3D and eased, carries the stickers into the new digits. Hour: a full scramble and speed-solve, the cube tumbling in the air. Exact, clean pixel-art rendering; 40x40 LEDs at 3 mm on one continuous lattice.

Pianola. The 32x8 strip is a piano keyboard (32 keys, black keys drawn higher); the 20x20 square above is a falling-notes roll (Synthesia / a player-piano roll) scrolling down onto the keys. Keys light when struck. The falling notes are arranged so the roll draws the numerals as it scrolls: the time is music. Minute turn: a phrase whose notes spell the new minute; hour: a Westminster-style chime and a glissando cascade carrying the hour. The lattice continues across the two boards, so notes fall straight onto their keys.

Rain on glass. The leaning tower of parallelograms is a tall window at night; the lattice's 61-degree slant is the angle of wind-driven rain. Behind the glass a blurred city: bokeh of street lights, a neon sign, passing car lights. Raindrops bead, merge and run in slanted rivulets; the numerals are written by water on the glass, drops gathering into the strokes and refracting the city light. Minute turn: a gust or a fat drop running down wipes the changed digit and new drops bead into the new one. Hour: lightning flash, a downpour sheet, then clearing. The seams between boards are window mullions.

Cuttlefish. The 32x16 panel is a close-up of a cuttlefish's skin. Chromatophores (yellow, red-brown, black pigment sacs) expand and contract, iridophores shimmer blue-green, and 'passing cloud' bands roll across the skin continuously. The animal writes the time in its skin: the digits are skin patterns. Minute turn: a passing-cloud wave sweeps across and the pattern morphs into the new digit. Hour: a full courtship display, zebra stripes pulsing and iridescence flaring, maybe an eye and tentacles entering the frame. Biologically real colour, mesmerising motion. One continuous lattice.

Mitosis. Two hexagons are two fields of view under a fluorescence microscope (DAPI-blue nuclei, GFP-green microtubules, red actin). In each lives a cell whose chromosomes condense into the shape of the digits: hours in the left cell, minutes in the right. Cytoplasm streams, vesicles drift. Minute turn: the cell goes through mitosis; the nuclear envelope dissolves, the spindle forms, chromatids are pulled apart, the cell pinches in two, and the daughter nucleus carries the new digits. Hour: both cells divide in sync and the fields fill with cells before clearing. Scientific beauty.

Pizza. Six triangles are six slices of a pizza; the gaps between the boards are the cuts and the hole in the middle is where the slices meet. Bubbling cheese, browning crust, steam. The time is made of toppings: pepperoni, olives, basil arranged into the numerals across the slices. Minute turn: a hand or a cheeky mouse lifts a slice with stretching cheese and the toppings rearrange into the next digit. Hour: the pizzaiolo spins the whole pizza, toppings fly and land as the new hour. Funny, warm. (Alternative if stronger: a camera iris of six blades.)

The Great Wave. A living ukiyo-e print after Hokusai: a Prussian-blue wave with claw-like white foam fingers, Mount Fuji small in the distance, boats in the trough. The wave builds and curls continuously; the numerals are written in the foam or the curl, or as brush digits in a woodblock cartouche. Minute turn: the wave breaks and the spray rearranges into the new digit. Hour: a giant wave swallows the print, the sea calms and the new hour appears with a red seal stamp. Ukiyo-e palette (Prussian blue, indigo, cream paper, a red seal). 40x20 at 3 mm, one continuous lattice.
